articles.title: Ronda Rousey announces shock return to mixed martial arts: 'This is for all MMA fans past, present and future'
articles.summary: Ronda Rousey will have her first mixed martial arts bout in a decade when she fights Gina Carano on May 16 in Los Angeles; "This is for all MMA fans past, present and future. More to come… much more," Rousey said; The event will be the first MMA bout staged by Jake Paul's MVP
articles.body:
It has been almost a decade since Rousey last competed in the UFC, but she will have her first MMA bout since 2016 when she fights Gina Carano on May 16 at the Intuit Dome in Los Angeles.

Rousey is a trailblazing mixed martial artist, with a record-setting career as the UFC's first and most dominant female fighter and bantamweight champion.

She was the first woman inducted into the UFC Hall of Fame and catapulted the women's WWE division towards its first WrestleMania main event in history.

Her return to the sport sees her fight Carano at 145lbs.

This event, the first MMA bout staged by Most Valuable Promotions, will be professionally sanctioned under the unified rules of MMA and contested over five five-minute rounds using 4oz gloves, inside a hexagon cage.

"Been waiting so long to announce this: me and Gina Carano are going to throw down in the biggest super-fight in women's combat sport history," Rousey said.

"This is for all MMA fans past, present and future. More to come… much more."

Carano said: "Ronda came to me and said there is only one person she would make a comeback for and it has been her dream to make this fight happen between us.

"She thanked me for opening up doors for her in her career and was respectful in asking for this fight to happen. This is an honour. I believe I will walk out of this fight with the win and I anticipate it will not come easy, which I welcome.

"This is as much for Ronda and me as it is for the fans and mixed martial arts community. What a time to be alive."

Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian, the co-founders of Most Valuable Promotions said: "MVP has always been driven by disruption and delivering the biggest moments in combat sports on a global scale, and today we are officially bringing that energy to MMA for the first time.

"MVP's conviction in women's boxing was driven by the success achieved by Ronda Rousey, who was the biggest star of the entire sport of MMA during her career.

"Ronda Rousey and Gina Carano are the two most formative figures in the history of women's MMA; they are the icons who shattered the glass ceiling and helped build the foundation this sport stands on."

articles.title: ONE Championship: Tomyamkoong Bhumjaithai achieves TKO victory over debutant Bejenuta 'Gladiator' Maximus
articles.summary: Tomyamkoong Bhumjaithai beat Moldova's Bejenuta 'Gladiator' Maximus with a third-round TKO; Isannuea Sor Sasiwat floored Khunpon Aekmuangnon with a left hook to the body for a first-round knockout
articles.body:
The victory eventually came by TKO at 1:41 of round three, but Tomyamkoong established his game plan early inside the iconic Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand.

Maximus, a 24-year-old debutant, threw some unorthodox punches and bounced in and out of range but Tomyamkoong stayed composed, picking his shots and refusing to be drawn in.

Maximus deployed counter-attacking tactics one again in the second round but Tomyamkoong tracked him until he found his opening, folding his opponent with a straight right to the body that buckled the knees.

Tomyamkoong stayed sharp and methodical in the third as the Moldovan toiled and Tomyamkoong cut off the ring and sent him down with a fierce left hand down the middle.

Maximus beat the eight-count but it was a brief reprieve, Tomyamkoong flew into the clinch and unleashed a relentless barrage of knees and elbows until the referee stepped in to end it.

Tomyamkoong now stands on 127 victories after stringing together three straight wins and cementing himself as a rising flyweight division contender.

Isannuea hits half-century with first round KO against Khunpon

Isannuea Sor Sasiwat needed fewer than three minutes to put away Khunpon Aekmuangnon, dropping the Thai with a devastating body shot KO in round one of the co-main event.

Isannuea was laser-focused from the get-go and followed flyweight rival Khunpon around the ring from the opening bell, whipping punches at him from every angle.

The 20-year-old backed up and found early comfort in his left kick, snapping it into Isannuea's guard as a counter to slow the incoming punches.

As he began to come forward, though, Isannuea read his intentions and let rip a left body hook that hit Khunpon's ribcage and sent him sprawling to the canvas.

With the finish, Isannuea earned his 50th win, recording back-to-back KO victories to put the flyweight division on notice.

articles.title: ONE Fight Night 42: Dzhabir Dzhabrailov emerges with comeback knockout victory as Sam-A Gaiyanghadao delivers masterclass
articles.summary: Turkish sensation Dzhabir Dzhabrailov authored a stunning first-round comeback to knock out American powerhouse Chase Mann while Muay Thai legend Sam-A Gaiyanghadao landed a breath-taking walk-off head-kick knockout of Elmehdi El Jamari in co-main event at ONE Fight Night 42.
articles.body:
Dzhabrailov had never been truly tested in his professional MMA career. Six battles, six finishes, and his last four ending in the first round.

The 21-year-old Turkish phenom faced his sternest examination yet against Chase "Mannimal" Mann in the main event of ONE Fight Night 42 - and although he encountered tremendous adversity along the way, he ultimately passed with flying colours.

Once the opening bell rang, Mann immediately took control of the action.

The American powerhouse dragged Dzhabrailov to the mat within seconds and pinned him against the ropes, showcasing the immense strength he previously amassed from his powerlifting days. When the young Turk scrambled to his feet, Mann greeted him with a vicious right hand that sent him crashing back down to the canvas.

'The Mannimal' attacked while the Turk was trying to stand up, as he unleashed a knee down the centre, peppered him with heavy rights, and then picked him up and dumped him in the corner. The 29-year-old followed that up with a plethora of short elbows, punches, and knees to the head.

Throughout his ONE Championship tenure, Dzhabrailov had never been threatened, and if he didn't try to remove himself from that dreadful position, his flawless reputation would be completely destroyed. Knowing this, he stood up in the corner, avoided his rival's single-leg takedown attempt, and circled away from him.

Mann continued punching his way into the takedown, but the tide was turning. The Turk fended him off, created some distance, and landed a few hard shots of his own. He even pushed him away with some front kicks.

Mann confidently stepped away, patiently waiting for his opponent to walk forward with the hope of landing the finishing blow. But it never came.

Instead, Dzhabrailov threw a wild right hand that missed entirely. But his momentum carried him through, his hips rotating perfectly as he unleashed a left hook that caught Mann flush on the button.

The American dropped like a stone. Dzhabrailov pounced, landing two hammerfists before referee Olivier Coste could pull him away at 2:31 of round one.

That surprising comeback victory extended Dzhabrailov's flawless record to 7-0 and marked his fifth consecutive first-round stoppage win. More crucially, he'd passed his toughest test under the brightest lights, proving he possesses the heart to match his devastating finishing ability.

Mann's record fell to 7-1 in his first professional defeat, and now, the Turkish wrecking machine has positioned himself for a shot at Christian Lee's ONE Welterweight MMA world title. However, whether he gets the nod remains to be seen.

Sam-A delivers masterclass in defying expectations

At 42 years old, Sam-A should be thinking about retirement. Instead, he's thinking about another crack at world title gold, and it is becoming more and more difficult to deny him.

The Thai legend produced a captivating second-round knockout of Elmehdi 'The Sniper' El Jamari in the strawweight Muay Thai co-main event, surviving a dramatic knockdown to land a walk-off head kick that left his Moroccan opponent spark out on the canvas.

El Jamari barrelled forward from the opening bell, throwing punches in bunches. His Western boxing background caused Sam-A problems early, a stiff right hand cracking off the veteran's skull. But the icon has seen every trick in the book across his 427 previous professional bouts. He remained patient, waiting for El Jamari's aggression to create openings.

The second round was absolute bedlam. Sam-A caught the 28-year-old Moroccan when he was flexing and knocked him down hard with a left hand. El Jamari climbed upright and answered the referee's eight-count, only for a straight right to put him flat on his back again.

One more knockdown, and the Thai icon would earn an automatic second-round TKO.

But somehow, El Jamari summoned the energy for one final rally. He charged forward recklessly, swinging wildly, and connected with a left hook of his own. Sam-A hit the deck as the Lumpinee Stadium crowd erupted in disbelief.

Legends, however. aren't built on winning when things go to plan. They're built on winning when everything goes wrong.

Sam-A stood back up, circled deliberately to his left, and waited. The duo mixed it up in the clinch, forcing the referee to separate them several times. But when the Moroccan lunged forward once more with a left hook, Sam-A's left leg whistled through the air, his shin crashing into El Jamari's temple with sickening precision.

The Moroccan crumbled instantly as the referee frantically stopped the match and the living legend celebrated his third straight victory.

But that wouldn't be the only reason for him to celebrate. Sam-A's shocking highlight-reel performance earned him a $50,000 performance bonus and could place him back into contention for the ONE Strawweight Muay Thai world title.

articles.title: UFC Freedom 250: Justin Gaethje stuns Ilia Topuria at White House event hosted by Donald Trump
articles.summary: UFC Freedom 250 was held on the South Lawn of the Washington DC complex, with fighters passing through the Oval Office; Ciryl Gane knocked out Alex Pereira to win the interim UFC heavyweight title; Sean O'Malley secured a knockout of Aiemann Zahabi in their bantamweight bout
articles.body:
The American had bloodied his Spanish-Georgian opponent with a left-right combination to the face in the third round, leading to an extended break after the round in which doctors seemed to suggest the fight should end.

Topuria's corner then called for the fight to be stopped after the fourth round.

After securing the UFC lightweight title Gaethje was greeted by President Donald Trump, who was hosting the event to celebrate his 80th birthday and the nation's 250th anniversary, in the Octagon.

In other fights, Ciryl Gane knocked out Alex Pereira to win the interim UFC heavyweight title.

French fighter Gane overcame the Brazilian after the referee stopped the action in the second round at 1:27, following a left to the chin.

Mr Trump held the event on the White House South Lawn with seven fights in total.

Sean O'Malley secured a knockout of Canadian Aiemann Zahabi in their bantamweight bout, saluting troops afterwards, while Diego Lopes knocked out Steve Garcia in a featherweight contest.

Mauricio Ruffy knocked out Michael Chandler in a lightweight contest, while Josh Hokit saw off Derrick Lewis in the second round of a heavyweight fight.

Earlier in the night, Bo Nickal knocked out Kyle Daukaus in the first round of their middleweight fight.

Fighters warmed up in different storied rooms of the capital landmark, each of them passing through the Oval Office on their way to the Octagon.

The unusual event also came just hours after Mr Trump confirmed a deal to end the war in Iran and allow oil traffic to begin again through the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Nico Carrillo: Huge-hitting 'King of the North' to return live on Sky Sports on August 15 in kickboxing contest
articles.summary: After a tremendous winning run culminated in capturing the ONE Interim Featherweight Muay Thai world title, Scotland's Nico Carrillo will compete next in a kickboxing bout; Watch Carrillo fight Zhou Jiaqiang live on Sky Sports on August 15
articles.body:
Scottish star Carrillo, a devastating force in Muay Thai, is taking on new ONE signing Zhou Jiaqiang in a featherweight kickboxing bout on ONE Fight Night 46 at the iconic Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand.

A hugely powerful striker, Carrillo, from Glasgow, is known as the "King of the North".

After establishing himself as one of the finest Muay Thai athletes on the continent, Carrillo embarked on a stunning run that left a trail of destruction through the UK and Europe. That run included winning the WBC Muay Thai European Championship.

The 11-fight winning streak was enough to catch ONE Championship's attention, and Carrillo's dominance continued on the proving grounds of ONE Friday Fights. His devastating power was on show during a pair of crushing knockout wins over Furkan Karabag and Muangthai PK Saenchai.

Those victories earned the Deachkalek Muay Thai Academy representative a coveted $100,000 contract to the world's largest martial arts organisation.

Eventually, the Scot earned a shot at the ONE Interim bantamweight Muay Thai world champion in January 2025, but he suffered a heartbreaking defeat to Nabil Anane. However, Carrillo took away some valuable lessons and moved up a division to compete in his natural weight class.

That decision was a game-changer. The Glasgow native defeated the legendary Sitthichai Sitsongpeenong and American standout Luke Lessei to earn his crack at the ONE Interim featherweight Muay Thai world title in February 2025.

Over the course of five rounds, he beat Shadow Singha Mawynn to finally strike world title gold and fulfill his dream.

Watch Nico Carrillo vs Zhou Jiaqiang in a featherweight kickboxing bout live on Sky Sports on August 15.

articles.title: Conor McGregor to undergo surgery on knee injury which ended return fight against Max Holloway at UFC 329 but hopes to fight again
articles.summary: Conor McGregor outlined a plan for surgery, rehabilitation and another fight following a knee injury in his UFC 329 fight with Max Holloway which lasted just 69 seconds
articles.body:
The ​former two-weight world champion suffered the injury in the opening moments of his ​fight with Holloway on Sunday in Las Vegas when he landed awkwardly after attempting a jump ​kick.

McGregor tried to fight on for a few seconds but looked towards the referee to signal ​he could not continue.

"All things work ⁠out for my good! All ⁠things are possible for me because I am a believer!" McGregor wrote ‌on Instagram. "Surgery. Prehab. Return to martial arts practice. Go again. Final fight of the contract. Please God!"

Speaking after the fight, UFC president Dana White said: "Five years off in this sport is rough.

"We're assuming a blown ACL. That's what I assumed when I saw it and that's what the doctors think too."

Asked if there may have been an existing injury, White said there were no signs of it at last Friday's ceremonial weigh-in. White added that, with the millions of social-media views of McGregor rushing Holloway at the weigh-in, someone would have noticed if anyone was injured.

On Sunday, McGregor's manager, John Kavanagh, said his client did not have a previous knee injury.

"That opening jump switch kick was drilled daily for months, multiple times in warm-up. Never an issue," Kavanagh wrote on Facebook.

"Knee went when he [threw] the very first kick. Doesn't get any worse than this."

Following the fight, McGregor also said he had no previous injury. "I was throwing kicks, planted and jumping, all throughout camp as well as backstage before the fight," McGregor said on X.

"I had no injury/injuries going into the fight."

Injuries ‌and issues away from the sport have derailed the 37-year-old Irishman's career.

After breaking his leg against Dustin Poirier five years ago, McGregor was slated to meet Michael ⁠Chandler in June 2024 but that ​was cancelled after McGregor suffered a broken ​toe in training.

Later that year a jury ​in an Irish civil court found him liable ⁠for the assault of Nikita Hand, who had accused McGregor of rape, in 2018.

In October 2025, he accepted an 18-month ban for "whereabouts failures" ⁠after he missed three attempts ​by Combat Sports Anti-Doping to collect biological samples ​from him in 2024. The ban was backdated and expired in March.

articles.title: ONE Championship: Stephen Irvine suffers brutal knockout by Suablack Tor Pran49 in showdown at ONE Fight Night 45
articles.summary: Stephen Irvine's quest for flyweight gold in the co-main event of ONE Fight Night 45 ended in defeat after a devasting elbow in the second round; the Scot now holds a 30-5 record after his defeat by one of Thailand's most experienced Muay Thai fighters
articles.body:
The Glasgow fighter was finished by a perfectly-timed elbow in the second round which earned his opponent the victory and the $50,000 performance bonus.

'El Matador', as he is known, was competing at a new weight class after stepping up from straweight and had been hoping to get a win over the 85-fight veteran to help propel a charge towards the ONE Championship flyweight Muay Thai world title.

And Irvine started well at Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium, evading Suablack's early boxing combinations before firing back with a crisp right hand that sent the Thai to the mat for an eight-count in the waning seconds of the opening round. For a moment, it looked like Irvine's pre-fight prediction of a knockout and a bonus might actually materialise.

It did, in fact, but sadly for him, it was the Thai southpaw who got it.

Irvine continued to apply pressure in the second round, walking his Thai rival down with punches, the occasional kick, and a few heavy elbows.

It all changed, though, nearly a minute into the frame when Suablack exploded forward with a left cross that knocked down the Scot and shifted the momentum.

Irvine answered the referee's eight-count and appeared completely level-headed, but the reprieve wouldn't last long.

The Scot moved forward in search of a knee strike, but Suablack retaliated with a body kick, another left cross, and then lunged forward with a powerful elbow that smashed Irvine's face with sickening precision and immediately crumbled him to the canvas.

Once again, the referee administered an eight-count, but when the Glasgow striker stumbled and failed to rise, the match was waved off.

For Irvine, fresh off earning a lucrative contract and a place on ONE Championship's global roster just nine months earlier, this was a harsh introduction to the flyweight division's elite. The move up in weight, which he'd convinced himself would play to his strengths, instead highlighted how much work remains before he can challenge for world title gold.

Suablack improved to 63-23 and announced himself as a genuine force in the flyweight Muay Thai division whereas Irvine will need to bounce back from a sobering defeat.

articles.title: Allan Nascimento: UFC fighter dies aged 34 after suffering apparent heart attack in his sleep
articles.summary: Allan Nascimento, the Brazilian flyweight, was found unresponsive on Monday; UFC pays tribute to "our beloved fighter and exemplary flyweight"
articles.body:
The Brazilian flyweight was found unresponsive on Monday after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep.

A UFC statement said: "This morning, Monday, August 3, our beloved fighter and exemplary flyweight Allan Nascimento was found unresponsive after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep.

"Despite the efforts of the responding medical team, he was pronounced deceased at the scene.

"Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Allan's family, friends, team-mates, and loved ones during this incredibly difficult time."

Nascimento, who had won 22 of his 29 bouts, last fought in June, when he lost to Mitch Raposo in Las Vegas on a split decision.

articles.title: Anthony Joshua: Heavyweight's former trainer has his say on what happens next in Tyson Fury fight negotiations
articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have been negotiating a blockbuster showdown later this year; Fury has "signed up" for the fight and is "just waiting for AJ", says his promoter Frank Warren; Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn says talks have "reopened" to stage the fight at Wembley Stadium
articles.body:
Frank Warren, who promotes Fury, told Sky Sports this week that terms were agreed and they were "waiting for AJ", while Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has announced that talks have reopened to stage the fight at Wembley Stadium .

But McCracken, who trained Joshua as an amateur and steered him to world heavyweight title glory as a professional, believes the two British stars should not pay any attention to the constant speculation about a long-awaited fight.

"I had a career as a fighter and you look back at what you maybe wished you should have done and what you shouldn't have done," McCracken exclusively told Sky Sports .

"I think it works out how it should work out most of the time, but it's up to the fighters if they want to fight each other and try and get the better of each other.

"I don't think it's anybody else's business whether they should fight or not - I think they both proved themselves.

"One thing I'd say is everyone's talking about it - it puts boxing on the map and it's great for boxing. While boxing's in the forefront and in the news, I think it's a really positive thing."

Fury expressed his frustration at the prolonged negotiations in a social media outburst, branding Joshua as a "coward" , but McCracken insists the Olympic gold medallist and former world champion would relish the chance to settle a fierce rivalry.

"With Anthony Joshua, in my experiences, he was happy to fight anybody," said McCracken. "It was just about how it was packaged and what was best for him - that's how the fighters look at things these days.

"I've not been involved for a long time with Joshua, but it looks like it's going to happen. Hopefully it will and then obviously everyone can enjoy it."

The fighters had differing fortunes in summer warm-up fights as Fury sealed a one-sided stoppage of Mariusz Wach, while Joshua had to climb off the canvas twice before halting Kristian Prenga.

But McCracken has suggested that Joshua will be fuelled by the criticism of his close scare.

He said: "Joshua is coming off the back of not a great performance, but obviously he got the knockout and that is all that really matters. He'll be looking to prove people wrong, any of the doubters.

"Tyson [Fury] would be the favourite at the moment with his recent results and his form. It's quite fascinating if you actually think about it, where it's got to and the time it's taken to actually get the fight on."

'A Night of Solidarity' - Olympic-style night to celebrate power of sport

McCracken was speaking to Sky Sports ahead of 'A Night of Solidarity' on November 13, a night of Olympic-style boxing to celebrate the unifying power of sport and raise funds for firefighters' charities, youth sport organisations and community groups in North Kensington.

The night has been created to recognise the actions of the local community in the aftermath of the Grenfell Tower tragedy, when local boxing and sports clubs came together to help the community rebuild, create safe spaces for young people and help everyone affected by this devastating event.

The London Fire Brigade Boxing Club (LFB) has worked with local communities across London to deploy the unifying power of sport to provide structure and purpose to the lives of young people, bringing them together with rank-and-file firefighters in boxing gyms in a show of solidarity and support.

'A Night of Solidarity' aims to celebrate both these endeavours and bring them together, recognising the important role played by both the LFB Boxing Club and those clubs in the areas most impacted by the Grenfell Tower fire.

The evening will raise funds for local sports charities, the Firefighter's Charity and will include 12 bouts of boxing that will see an LFB Select team take on a North Kensington team, made-up of men, women and youth boxers from a variety of clubs in the local area and across London.

articles.title: Katie Taylor ecstatic after beating Flora Pili to make perfect end to ‘dream career’ at Dublin's Croke Park
articles.summary: Katie Taylor beats Flora Pili in the final fight of her boxing career, becoming an undisputed world champion for the third time; the judges score it 100-90, 100-90, 98-91 as Taylor headlines first boxing event at Croke Park since Muhammad Ali fought Al “Blue” Lewis in 1972.
articles.body:
Taylor outclassed Flora Pili in a unanimous points victory in front of a crowd of 80,000 to ensure her three decades as an amateur and professional boxer ended in fairytale fashion.

Wild celebrations followed the announcement that she had overwhelmed the previously unbeaten Pili 100-90 100-90 98-91 on the scorecards.

For Taylor the feeling of signing off in front of her fans bettered winning Olympic gold at London 2012, headlining Madison Square Garden and her trilogy against Amanda Serrano.

The 40-year-old said: "This was definitely the highlight of my whole career.

"I didn't think anything could get bigger than London 2012 and then MSG came along.

"I didn't think anything could get bigger than that first fight with Serrano and then here we are at Croke Park.

"I ended my career on top, like every athlete wants to do, on my terms, and I ended it as the undisputed champion.

"That's exactly how I wanted it to end. It was so important to me all along to end my career well."

Taylor thrilled Croke Park with a spine-tingling ring walk and also delivered in the ring by outclassing Pili across all 10 rounds.

She finished the fight by launching an all-out assault in the final 10 seconds that was roared on by the crowd and once the bell sounded, she smiled and hugged her opponent knowing she had thrown her final shots.

Taylor said: "This night was everything I expected and more. Thankfully I was able to hold my emotions together because I was getting emotional all week speaking about this event.

"And over the last few months, the preparation for this has been so emotional. But the atmosphere was so special. It was beyond my wildest dreams. It was unbelievable.

"What an amazing night. Looking back on an amazing career, this was just a dream ending to a dream career for me. What a way to end.

"I don't think there's another country in the world that would sell 80,000 tickets for a female athlete. I'm convinced Ireland was the only country that would actually do that.

"What a way to end this amazing journey. I started off this career and I had the dream of becoming an Olympic champion.

"I achieved that, but then these last 10 years have been beyond my wildest dreams. It's been a remarkable 10 years.

Taylor is open to remaining in Irish boxing in some capacity, providing she can convince her husband Sean McCavanagh to relocate from Connecticut where they are based.

But wherever her path leads, the Bray Bomber's place in Irish sporting immortality is assured after the nation paid homage to a trailblazer in women's sport.

"The whole country have seen my good times and also seen me during my devastation as well," Taylor said.

"I think people really resonate with your vulnerabilities as much as your successes. They saw me cope with the heartbreak of the Rio Olympics.

"They saw me cope with the heartbreak of the Chantelle Cameron loss. This country has seen my personal difficulties as well.

"My story is the story of everybody in this room, everybody in the whole country. We all have our good days, our bad days. Life is full of ups and downs.

"We all have seasons of trouble, seasons of success, but my disappointments and my struggles have always been in the limelight as well.

"I don't know why the adoration is there, but I'm just super grateful that it's there. I'm super grateful for this nation and for the dream for which we're here."

Hearn: Greatest Irish sportsperson of all time

"We went into this event and I said this will be the greatest atmosphere and greatest occasion boxing has ever seen and Croke Park, you did it tonight.

"There were 83,000 people in here tonight and they are still here. I wasn't supposed to do something we haven't done before. This is a woman who refused to take no as an answer and banged on every door. She's the greatest Irish sportsperson of all time.

"She made this happen. She made it happen because the entire nation supported her so proudly."

articles.title: Thomas Carty expects David Allen disqualification after bizarre end to fight on Katie Taylor undercard
articles.summary: Thomas Carty dramatically toppled through the ropes after being hit on the back of the head in the opening round of his clash with David Allen on the undercard of Katie Taylor's fight at Croke Park on Saturday; the bout was declared a 'no contest' after Carty was unable to continue
articles.body:
Carty dramatically toppled through the ropes after being hit on the back of the head in the opening round of his clash with Allen on the undercard of Katie Taylor's farewell fight at Croke Park on Saturday.

The bout was declared a 'no contest' after Carty was unable to continue, but Ofo believes Allen should have been penalised for an illegal blow.

Ofo told Sky Sports : "I am very disappointed about what happened on Saturday night at Croke Park and the untimely halt to what should have been the crowning achievement of Thomas' career so far.

"Thomas was pumped to be fighting on such an historic event in front of such an enormous crowd at the home of Irish sport and was gutted by the bizarre turn of events.

"What happened was plain for all to see with Allen blatantly fouling him twice in quick succession in response to Thomas' punishing jab that immediately marked up Allen's face.

"The second, illegal rabbit punch to the back of Thomas' head knocked him clean through the ropes and there is only one outcome under the rules of boxing in those circumstances - a DQ loss for Allen."

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Allen had attempted to explain the final punch of the fight by saying: " I went up a bit close, caught him with a left hook to the body and rattled him a little bit to the head.

"I think, then he threw a combination, knocked my head back with an uppercut.

"But then he grabbed me frantically. I'm not aiming for the back of anyone's head ever, but I am aiming about here [the ear].

"It wasn't a big shot; I tried to clip him round the ear as I always do, and he's turned his head into it. It's gone round the back of the head.

"From there on, I don't know. It's not for me to say what's happened. He's a good guy, I do like him...

"I've caught him behind the head, not on purpose; he's turned into, and he's gone through the ropes.

"At the time, I said to the referee, 'Are you not going to count?' If that was in the middle of the ring, I'd have won by stoppage."

But Ofo has dismissed Allen's account and is confident that Carty would have been victorious by stoppage if the fight had not ended prematurely.

The unfortunate ending to the fight was another cruel twist of luck for Carty, who endured his sole defeat last year after suffering a freakish knee injury, but the 30-year-old hopes to record his 12th professional win in a rematch with Allen.

Ofo said: "I see he is already busy trying to set a narrative but that is gaslighting and Thomas and the team were all confident that he would have stopped Allen in the later rounds, particularly in light of the terrible shape Allen turned up in. Frankly, he should change his nickname from 'The White Rhino' to 'The White Hippo.'

"However, once the BUI have reconsidered the referee's decision and done the right thing, we will happily give Allen a rematch and they can settle it once and for all - hopefully inside the ring this time!"

Allen declined to comment on Ofo's comments.

articles.title: Conor Benn hits out at Ryan Garcia for 'bottling it' after American fails to show up for face-off in Las Vegas
articles.summary: Conor Benn will challenge Ryan Garcia for his WBC welterweight belt on Saturday night in Las Vegas; it will be the first time Benn has contested for a world title in his career and is relishing being the underdog
articles.body:
The two fighters were scheduled to meet for a media opportunity at Mandalay Bay Hotel on Tuesday, but Benn was the only one to appear.

He was joined by his father, Nigel, and, with Garcia absent, Benn jokingly squared up to his dad, who appeared to mock the WBC welterweight titleholder, telling his son: "I'm not Ryan, I turn up!"

Benn, 29, will challenge for a world title for the first time in his career on Saturday night at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, hoping to emulate the achievements of his world champion father, who won the WBO middleweight title in 1990 and the WBC super-middleweight title in 1992.

Garcia, meanwhile, is set to make the first defence of his title, but was handed a stern warning by Benn ahead of their meeting.

"Saturday can't come soon enough," Benn said on Tuesday.

"I apologise for Ryan [Garcia] doing what Ryan does and bottling it. We turn up, we're here, ready for the face-off.

"He needs to get his s*** together because come Saturday, he's in for a real, real shock."

Ben comes into this fight off the back of successive victories. His first came in November 2025, when the English fighter exacted revenge on Chris Eubank Jr, after suffering the first professional defeat of his career against his rival in April of that year.

He returned to the ring in April 2026 and outscored Regis Prograis at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium to extend his fight record to 25-1.

Garcia represents a step up in opponent for Benn, with the 28-year-old American having secured his WBC welterweight belt following his dominant unanimous victory against Mario Barrios in February.

But Benn is relishing his status as the underdog, and following a protracted war of words with the American, he wants to end their verbal feud once and for all.

"I like being the underdog," Benn said. "I think I perform at my best.

"I think every single one of my fights has led me to this moment. All the pressure I've had early on in my career has prepared me for nights like those at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

"It's prepared me for the noise and the drama and the chaos. So come September 12, it's nothing new, nothing different."

articles.title: Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn: American reveals why he snubbed face-off, as Brit says he 'went through hell' to make weight
articles.summary: Ryan Garcia was criticised by Conor Benn after he failed to show up for a face-off with the British fighter on Tuesday, ahead of their much-anticipated WBC welterweight showdown in Las Vegas on Saturday
articles.body:
Garcia is set to embark on the first defence of his WBC welterweight title against Benn at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Saturday night.

Earlier in the week, the pair were due to meet at the Mandalay Bay Hotel for a media event, but the American fighter did not show up, with Benn subsequently claiming his opponent had "bottled it".

During a press conference on Wednesday, Garcia said: "I wasn't there because I didn't want to be.

"Look, we have a face-off at the press conference [Thursday], then at the weigh-ins [Friday] and then a final face-off literally in the ring when the refs give you instructions.

"I've been doing this for so long. I've had fight weeks in Vegas before. I've never had to do a face-off on [Tuesday]. So I have a routine to do, and it's just something I didn't want to do.''

"It was funny seeing him [Benn] staring at himself."

Benn, meanwhile, believes Garcia's absence let the fans down.

"Ultimately it's disrespectful to the public because they deserve it,'' he said on Wednesday.

"The public deserves us giving you guys the best. This is what we do. This is what we're here for.''

Benn: Weight cut dragged me through the pits of hell

Benn comes into this fight as the underdog after stepping up to middleweight to fight Chris Eubank Jr. He lost his first fight against his rival in April 2025, before avenging that loss later that November. He comes into this weekend's bout after beating Regis Prograis at a 150lbs catchweight in April.

Should Benn make the weight at Friday's weigh-in, this will be the first time that he has fought at the welterweight limit in over four years, with his last fight at under 147lbs coming against Chris van Heerden in April 2022.

The 29-year-old hit back at those who have doubted his ability to make the weight, but added he felt like he had been "dragged through the pits of hell and had a fight with satan" during his preparations.

"A lot of people said I couldn't make the weight, watch me do it," Benn said, adding he went through 15 weeks of dieting before the fight.

Benn added that this would be his last fight at 147lbs and is hoping to move up in weight after this to 160 or 168lbs.

Garcia said he didn't want to hear any excuses from Benn after the fight regarding his weight cut.

"All we can do is go by past experience," Garcia said. "He cut back down to 150lbs to fight Regis Prograis. We have seen how he bloated up. Now he has an extra three pounds to go. I don't want to hear any excuses. He doesn't have a rehydration clause.

"I don't want to be hearing any crybaby s*** from him. He's trying to set up a narrative, because when he gets his a** whopped, he'll say: 'I was drained'. I'm about to beat his a**, it doesn't matter how much he weighs."

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Fight is '100 per cent happening' says Fury's manager as Cardiff emerges as potential venue
articles.summary: Cardiff and Wembley among three potential venues for the all-British super-fight, says Tyson Fury’s manager; Spencer Brown "100 per cent that the fight will happen" with negotiations still ongoing between both camps
articles.body:
The long-awaited British blockbuster fight has been stuck in negotiations in recent months amid an apparent disagreement over the location for the event with Joshua's team having remained insistent it must take place in the UK.

Fury's manager Spencer Brown is confident the fight will still happen - and on home soil, potentially in December.

"It's inching closer and it looks like it could be the British Boxing Bonanza that we all hoped for taking place in Britain," Brown told Sky Sports .

"Three venues are still under consideration with Cardiff and Wembley still in the running.

"It's looking good, Tyson has been onboard with fighting AJ since the start and he will fight him anywhere.

"November and December are both in play but we like December as an option, everyone would be winding up work for the holidays, it would be the best Christmas party in the world."

Brown added: "I'm 100 per cent that the fight will happen.

"Everyone is still in negotiations, Eddie Hearn and Frank Warren are both onboard but I'm fully confident we can get it done, of course the final say with be with Turki Al-Sheikh, Netflix and SELA but we are on track to getting it done."

Matchroom's Eddie Hearn has meanwhile reiterated his desire to deliver the fight in front of a UK audience.

He told Sky Sports: "We continue to do everything we can to bring this fight to the UK. We are in constant communication with Netflix and SELA - keep your fingers crossed."

A spokesperson for the Welsh Rugby Union told Sky Sports in July: "We'd be delighted to host this fight.

"We are very keen to attract more boxing to the stadium, which has a rich history in the sport, enhanced by its closable roof, unrivalled sight lines and unique city-centre location."

articles.title: Ryan Garcia targets world championship unification with Teofimo Lopez next | ‘Conor Benn will be back’
articles.summary: Ryan Garcia handed Conor Benn a vicious two-round defeat in Las Vegas, but Garcia believes Benn will be able to come back: "He needs to be a little bit more patient. I have a new level of respect for him"; Garcia will look to fight American rival Teofimo Lopez next
articles.body:
Garcia looked imperious as he dismissed Benn inside two rounds at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.

But the American superstar believes Benn can rebuild and recover.

"He just needs to gain a little bit more experience. I don't think he has enough experience at this point. I don't think he was as experienced as me but I think he will be back. He went in, tried to fight me," Garcia said.

"You can't jump in like that. It's not the move. I think that he needs to be a little bit more patient.

"He's an alright dude. I have a new level of respect for him. I hope he can come back and do great things in the sport."

After defending the WBC welterweight title, Garcia immediately had words for WBA champion Teofimo Lopez, who was in attendance at the arena.

"I want to unify against Teofimo. I think that's the move," Garcia said afterwards. "It's a huge fight and Teo's an entertaining dude and it's going to be a hell of a build-up and he's a good fighter too so let's run it."

Lopez, who has past wins over Vasiliy Lomachenko and Josh Taylor on his stellar resume, was soundly beaten by Shakur Stevenson earlier this year. But Lopez bounced back to beat Rolando Romero, who himself beat Garcia last year.

But Garcia warned: "I was just getting started in there [against Benn]. There's a lot of things that I've been working on. But that's just another opportunity to show that in another fight.

"I have a lot of weapons in my arsenal that I didn't bring out yet."

articles.title: Caroline Dubois sets course for undisputed championship fight with 'jealous, threatened' Alycia Baumgardner
articles.summary: With American rival Alycia Baumgardner challenging Elif Nur Turhan for IBF lightweight title, WBO and WBC champion Caroline Dubois wants to unify against WBA title holder Stephanie Han; Watch Elif Nur Turhan vs Alycia Baumgardner on November 9 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Baumgardner will challenge Elif Nur Turhan for the IBF lightweight world title, live on Sky Sports in the early hours of Monday November 9.

Dubois, the unified WBC and WBO 135lb champion, expects to fight the winner for the undisputed crown but doesn't want to wait on the sidelines. She intends to add another belt to her collection and is targeting Stephanie Han, the WBA belt-holder, next.

"I want to become undisputed and I want to be involved in relevant fights. To unify the division is my dream right now. The only other champion [available] is Han and we'll just have to see if I can get it in before the end of the year. If not we'll have to go early next year," Dubois told Sky Sports .

"Hopefully we'll be unified world champion by the end of this year or early next. One belt away from becoming undisputed."

Dubois completed a successful defence of her titles when she beat Amelia Moore in Birmingham last month and immediately afterwards engaged Baumgardner in a furious war of words.

"She's most definitely intimidated by me. She's frightened of what I bring to the table. When she looks at me I know that she sees a younger, better, stronger, more talented, more everything better than her. Everything I do is just better than her. I feel like she's threatened by that," Dubois said.

"Everything that she has had to work so hard to get I've had it and I've achieved it in such quick succession. She's threatened, she's jealous. She's feeling a lot of emotions and all I can say is I hope she can focus herself, get that win [over Turhan] and we can find out who's the best.

"I hope she wins the fight. I'm going to be real upset if she doesn't win because I need to show her something," Dubois continued.

"Elif Turhan, the champion, versus Alycia Baumgardner, the contender, is going to be an awesome fight. I want the winner. I've made it very clear. I feel like I have been very vocal about the fact that I want to become undisputed.

"The path has revealed itself to me. The path has become clear now... So close, but so far."

articles.title: Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton fight time, ringwalks, undercard and how to watch or stream live on Sky Sports
articles.summary: Johnny Fisher returns to heavyweight action at the Copper Box against Belgium's determined Michael Pirotton, with Craig Richards vs Radivoje Kalajdzic, Lee Cutler vs Louis Greene and much more on the card; Watch Zuffa Boxing 11 on September 26 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Heavyweight hitter Johnny Fisher is looking to kickstart a surge up the ranks, while Belgium's Pirotton is determined to make a name for himself against the hugely popular "Romford Bull".

Their fight headlines Zuffa Boxing 11 at the Copper Box Arena in London that sees a raft of 50-50 fights and unbeatens matched against one another.

Fisher and Pirotton will collide on Saturday September 26, live on Sky Sports.

Live coverage of the action-packed bill in London starts at 7pm on Sky Sports .

Preliminary bouts will be streamed on Sky's digital platforms from 5pm.

Zuffa Boxing 11 takes places at the Copper Box Arena in London.

Fisher has 14 professional wins against one defeat. A hard puncher, he has taken 12 of those wins inside the distance, giving him a knockout ratio of over 85%.

Pirotton has been beaten twice and has 12 pro wins, six of them inside the distance. The Belgian's losses both came against opponents who were undefeated at the time.

The Fisher vs Pirotto ringwalks are expected to take place between 9.45 and 10.15pm.

Fisher told Sky Sports : "It's a golden ticket for Michael Pirotton, but it's also my golden ticket because if I win, I get to go on to bigger and better things. I've got ambitions in this game.

"You want to get the knockout, you want to get the stoppage, but I've always said from the beginning of my career, I've got to win by whatever cost - the win is the most important thing.

"But with my power, my strength, my explosivity, of course I can draw a knockout or draw a stoppage.

"Once I get someone hurt, I know I can finish them. I can smell when someone's feeling it or in trouble."

Pirotton told Sky Sports : "He's a tough guy, he's strong guy, he's a decent guy, but he can't knock me out.

"I'm not over and it's not over until I say it's over."

Zuffa Boxing 11 also features former world light-heavyweight title challenger Craig Richards against Radivoje "Hot Rod" Kalajdzic in the chief support.

British middleweights Lee Cutler and Louis Greene will go to war in an all-action bout.

Unbeaten Preston prospect Leon Hughes will box 10-3 light-heavyweight Michael Stephenson .

Cesar Mateo Tapia , unbeaten in 19 pro contests, takes on Leo Ruiz , a Mexican based in California with a 17-1 record.

Kayla Allen will make her professional debut while Alex MacMillan will look to continue his winning run against 2-0 Frenchman Guillaume Azagier .

London-based Moldovan Aurel Ignat , who shocked Scott Forrest with a first-round KO win last year, will put his unbeaten record on the line against Mexican Olympian Rogelio Romero , a 6-0 prospect from Juarez who has a 100 per cent knockout ratio.

Fred Pullen , a national champion as an amateur, makes his pro debut against Italy's Leonardo Faretina and in a clash of unbeaten prospects, America's Alexis De La Cerda meets Ireland's Cain Lewis .

articles.title: Asian Games 2026 Day 2: India win four medals as shooting delivers three and Suchika Tariyal makes MMA history amid heartbreak
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: Gold continued to elude India, but medals kept coming on the second day of the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya as the country added four more t.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Gold continued to elude India, but medals kept coming on the second day of the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya as the country added four more to its tally on Monday.Three came from the shooting range, while Suchika Tariyal created history by becoming India’s first Asian Games medallist in mixed martial arts. Her bronze, however, came with heartbreak after a closely fought semifinal ended in a draw, with her higher weight denying her a place in the final.India now have six medals — four silver and two bronze — after two days of competition, but are still waiting for their first gold.Shooting delivers three more medalsThe shooting range once again proved to be India’s biggest source of medals.Himanshu Dhillon won silver and Rudrankksh Patil took bronze in the men’s 10m air rifle individual event, while both were part of the Indian team that secured silver in the team competition alongside 18-year-old Parth Mane.The trio combined for 1898.4 points, but China raised the bar yet again. Sheng Lihao, Changhong Zhang and Sihan Ma amassed 1899.0 to win gold and set a new world record, improving the previous mark of 1898.4 set in Cairo last year.For India, the individual medals added another layer to an impressive day for the young shooters. Dhillon, 21, and Mane, 18, are still finding their feet at senior level, while Rudrankksh has already established himself as a major international contender.The three medals took India’s shooting tally to five — four silver and one bronze — after the country’s opening-day silver medals.ALSO READ: Why Suchika Tariyal lost despite a draw: How 700g denied India’s MMA fighter a historic final and left her in tearsSuchika makes history, but heartbreak followsSuchika Tariyal became the first Indian to win an Asian Games medal in MMA, but the historic bronze was not enough to hide her disappointment.The 36-year-old was involved in a tense semifinal against Singapore’s Hui Hoon Teo in the women’s traditional 60kg category. The bout ended in a draw, but MMA rules allow the lighter fighter to progress when the contest is level.Suchika was around 700 grams heavier than her opponent at the morning weigh-in and therefore missed out on a place in the final.She broke down in tears after the bout, knowing how close she had come to fighting for gold.Yet her bronze remains a landmark achievement. A resident of Kiloi village in Haryana’s Rohtak district, Suchika is a 2024 world champion in jiu-jitsu and has also represented India in judo at the 2022 Commonwealth Games and in kurash at the 2022 Asian Games.“This is more than my life. I will never forget that I came to Japan and got a medal for my country. I can now happily die,” Suchika told PTI after regaining her composure.India’s other MMA entrant, Varun Sanyal, had earlier been forced to withdraw from the competition after passing out during a sauna session while attempting to cut weight.Strong performances across team sportsThere was plenty for India to celebrate beyond the medal tally.The women’s hockey team continued its dominant start with a 17-1 rout of Indonesia in Pool B. The defending champions in kabaddi also began strongly, with the women defeating Bangladesh 42-21 and the men beating Japan 49-24.India’s badminton campaign got off to a similarly convincing start. The men swept Bangladesh 3-0 in the opening round, with Lakshya Sen, K Srikanth and Ayush Shetty winning their singles matches to make the remaining doubles matches unnecessary.The table tennis teams also delivered identical 3-0 wins over Pakistan. The women’s team topped Group F with their third straight victory, while the men bounced back from their defeat to Iran by completing a clean sweep of Pakistan.In boxing, Sumit Kundu produced an emphatic start in the men’s 70kg category, defeating Thailand’s Bunjong Sinsiri 5-0.Wushu also produced positive results, with Roshibina Devi and Aryan progressing to their respective quarterfinals.Swimming continues to disappointSwimming once again proved to be a difficult campaign for India.Two-time Olympian Srihari Nataraj finished 10th in the men’s 50m backstroke final. He clocked 25.52 seconds, slower than his 25.37 effort in the heats earlier in the day.Several other Indian swimmers failed to progress from their heats, including Akash Mani and Heer Gitesh Shah in the men’s 50m freestyle and Dhanush Suresh in the men’s 100m breaststroke.There was disappointment in soft tennis too. Aadhya Tiwari and Jay Meena’s mixed doubles campaign ended in the round of 16 after a hard-fought defeat to the Philippines’ Christy Sanosa and Sherwin Ray Nuguit.Four medals, but gold still elusiveIndia’s second day produced a mixture of history, heartbreak and encouraging performances across disciplines.The shooting range again provided the medals, while Suchika’s bronze ensured India entered the record books in MMA. The strong starts in hockey, kabaddi, badminton, table tennis, boxing and wushu offered further positives.But the elusive gold remains the biggest talking point.After two days, India have six medals — four silver and two bronze. The challenge now is to convert the strong starts and near misses into gold as the Asian Games move deeper into competition.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Paddy Pimblett vuelve a atacar a Ilia Topuria: "Es un perdedor"
articles.standfirst: El peleador inglés ha criticado a 'El Matador' por sus recientes declaraciones sobre Gaethje
articles.summary: El peleador inglés ha criticado a 'El Matador' por sus recientes declaraciones sobre Gaethje
articles.body: Las palabras de Ilia Topuria sobre Justin Gaethje no han caído en saco roto. Hace unos días, 'El Matador' provocó al estadounidense afirmando que la próxima vez mandaría revisar mejor sus guantillas, dejando caer que en el UFC Casa Blanca pudo hacer trampas. Como era de esperar, las respuestas no han tardado en llegar, y la última ha sido la de Paddy Pimblett, archienemigo y posible rival en un futuro del peleador hispanogeorgiano. Esta opinión de Topuria buscaba la reacción de todas las partes implicadas, pero el impacto que ha tenido ha sido incluso más grande. Gaethje se ha mostrado dispuesto a darle la revancha, la Comisión Atlética ha salido al paso de las acusaciones y hasta otros rivales de Ilia han opinado al respecto. Paddy sabe lo que es enfrentarse a Justin, hasta el punto de que también perdió contra él y su rostro también quedó notablemente dañado. Por tanto, el 'scouser' no solo no se cree las palabras de Ilia, sino que le ha criticado duramente a través de su canal de Youtube. “La comisión te observa mientras te vendan las manos. Ilia solo es un perdedor resentido. Está siendo un pequeño mari*** al respecto", afirmó. Las palabras de Paddy tampoco son casualidad, ya que sabe que es más que probable que se enfrente a Topuria en un futuro no tan lejano. La victoria de Arman Tsarukyan por K.O. ante Mauricio Ruffy en el UFC 331 ha colocado al armenio en un posición muy favorable para ser el siguiente retador al cinturón. De hecho, todo hace indicar que la última palabra la tendrá la UFC, ya que hay varias opciones sobre la mesa. Tsarukyan ha alzado la voz para pedir medirse a Gaethje. De hecho, a nivel mediático la compañía podría realizar el duelo entre Tsarukyan vs Gaethje y Topuria vs Pimblett y se aseguraría dos supercombates para 2027. A pesar de que no sería una pelea por el cinturón, el combate entre el inglés y el peleador hispanogeorgiano se vendería solo por la rivalidad que llevan manteniendo durante años y porque ambos son dos de las mayores superestrellas de la UFC. Por si fuera poco, definiría al siguiente retador al cinturón una vez se realizase el Tsarukyan vs Gaethje. La parte mala de esta opción es que si el estadounidense cae ante Arman seguramente se retire, por lo que Topuria jamás se podría vengar de su única derrota profesional. Hasta 2027 ni Gaethje ni Ilia volverán al octágono, así que de momento habrá que esperar para conocer las intenciones de la promotora.

articles.title: Lee Cutler beat one McKenna, now he wants to fight world champion brother Aaron McKenna if he can overcome Louis Greene
articles.summary: Lee Cutler will fight Louis Greene in an all-action middleweight clash at the Copper Box Arena on Saturday live on Sky Sports; Cutler is looking to launch himself into the world title picture, eyeing a fight with Aaron McKenna after already beating Stevie McKenna
articles.body:
Cutler overcame Stevie McKenna in a thriller in 2024. He lost a technical decision to Sam Eggington in another exciting match-up. Now looking to roar back to form, Cutler stopped Aaron Sutton in a Bournemouth homecoming and will take on Louis Greene next.

Greene, a hard puncher, has a tremendous aggressive style of fighting too. Cutler and Greene will collide at the Copper Box Arena on Saturday, live on Sky Sports .

"It's a dangerous fight," Cutler told Sky Sports . "I don't say no. It's a fight that the fans want to see and it's fight that I believe takes me to another level.

"[Greene is] tough. Punches extremely hard. I've got to be switched on for the full 10 rounds that we're in there. I'm fully prepared for a hard night.

"It's one of those fights, we're a stepping stone for each other and that's how we've got to see each other," he added.

"I've got to be smart in there and box how I know I can box. If I can do that I'll come away with the victory."

He had been expecting Stevie McKenna to look for a rematch with him.

McKenna levelled Owen O'Neill on the undercard of brother Aaron McKenna's IBF middleweight world title victory.

"It does surprise me. I thought I was going to get a callout after. I thought he might not want to fight me on the Dublin card because it's a big night for the family because of the brother and stuff," Cutler reflected.

"But I was fully expecting him to get through his opponent and then call me out after that. But the fact he didn't even mention my name, goes to show what he's about."

If he can get through his middleweight 10 rounder with Greene he will look for an eventual fight with new champion Aaron McKenna.

"I think he's very good. I think he's a tough fight for anyone. But he's somebody that I see myself in there with. Bring him on," Cutler declared.

"But as I said I'm focusing fully on Louis Green because he's a very dangerous opponent and if I take my eye off the ball for one second, anything can happen.

"I'm a come forward fighter, he's a come forward fighter, he's a huge puncher, very dangerous.

"All he has to do is touch somebody and then it's lights out."

articles.title: MMA pound-for-pound rankings (Sept. 2026): Joshua Van soars after UFC 331, Arman Tsarukyan crashes top 10
articles.summary: Van breaks into elite company in the pound-for-pound rankings with his dominant showing against Alexandre Pantoja, while Tsarukyan and another familiar name...
articles.body:
He's just 24 years old, but Joshua Van has proven a quick study in the mixed martial arts. If you thought his first encounter with Alexandre Pantoja was a fluky way to win a title, at UFC 331 the young gun left no doubt. He schooled the former flyweight champion en route to a dominant unanimous decision, which raises his stock in the pound-for-pound rankings big time.

Also on a northbound trek on the men's side of the rankings is Arman Tsarukyan, whose first-round knockout of Mauricio Ruffy may have finally punched his ticket to a lightweight title shot. He makes his return to the Uncrowned pound-for-pound list.

On the women's side, is that Alexa Grasso making her move? And with Amanda Nunes back with a fight scheduled for UFC 334 , the former pound-for-pound queen reappears, as if by magic, on this sacred list.

The panel of Ben Fowlkes, Chuck Mindenhall, Shaheen Al-Shatti, Petesy Carroll, Drake Riggs, Eric Jackman and Conner Burks have ranked both the men's and women's pound-for-pound best, one through 10, using a weighted points system to determine the final rankings (being voted No. 1 equals 10 points, No. 2 equals nine points, down to No. 10 equaling one point).

Our only criterion for these monthly rankings is that a fighter has competed within at least a calendar year of the publication date or has at least had a fight booked within that window. If a fighter hasn't competed in a year and books a fight after that time, he or she is once again eligible to be voted back in. Fighters who retire are no longer eligible for the rankings.

Though most of the best fighters are currently in the UFC, these rankings are not UFC exclusive. We take into consideration all the major promotions, from PFL and RIZIN to ONE Championship and MVP.

Without further ado, here are Uncrowned's MMA pound-for-pound rankings for September 2026!

1. Islam Makhachev — UFC welterweight champion (Prev: 1)

There are three names awaiting in front of Islam Makhachev, each one a little more harrowing than the last. There's Carlos Prates, who looks like he'll be next for the welterweight champion. There's Michael Morales, a hulking phenom biding his time. And there's Shavkat Rakhmonov, who remains on the mend. Not an easy slate.

2. Petr Yan — UFC bantamweight champion (Prev: 4)

Getting the UFC 333 trilogy with Merab Dvalishvili in Abu Dhabi is a boon for Yan, who has turned in some of his best work there, beating the likes of Jose Aldo, Cory Sandhagen and, most importantly, Marcus McGhee in signaling he was back. There are those who may still think Merab beat himself back in December, and this is the chance to move those narratives into the "cold takes" pile.

3. Alexander Volkanovski — UFC featherweight champion (Prev: 3)

It's admirable that Volkanovski was the lone advocate for Movsar Evloev to get a crack at his belt, but then again that's the nature of one of the UFC's steadiest presences. Here's guessing Volk craves new blood as much as the next guy, and the champ is confident he can do what no featherweight has done before. That is, serve Evloev up a big fat L.

4. Joshua Van — UFC flyweight champion (Prev: 10)

Listen man, Van has heard your criticisms. He's seen the words "freak injury" all over the headlines, and he's heard the word "fluke" being used in regard to his title. What he did by beating Pantoja fair and square was mute those conversations. It's now Van standing alone, without asterisks, atop the flyweight division. The future is wide open for the UFC's young star.

5. Justin Gaethje — UFC lightweight champion (Prev: 6)

Gaethje was a kind of co-star for UFC 331, in large part because Ilia Topuria began firing shots at him on social media, and also because Arman Tsarukyan solidified his standing as a contender to Gaethje's title. What happens next is up to the UFC, but MMA's potential Fighter of the Year might want to cherish that accessory while he has it.

6. Merab Dvalishvili — Former UFC bantamweight champion (Prev: 7)

Longest. Ten. Months. Of. His. Life. Last September, Merab had already defended the bantamweight title twice and was into a camp for a fight with Cory Sandhagen. This year he's had to keep busy with RAF wrestling matches as he waits out Yan's timetable for a return. The good news is, October is almost here.

7. Ilia Topuria — Former UFC lightweight champion (Prev: 8)

It was perhaps an act of pure cunning to reintroduce himself into the land of the living by declaring he's back just as Arman Tsarukyan was trying to punch his ticket for a title shot. But it was also a masterstroke to claim that Gaethje had something on his gloves. You know why? Because it got under Gaethje's skin, that's why.

8. Sean Strickland — UFC middleweight champion (Prev: 9)

Strickland can't help himself. He gets antsy. During UFC 331, he was on his X feed doing Sean Strickland things. One of his posts read, "I love MMA but I want to box.. Prefer Zuffa but if they cant make that happen....." He said it just like that, with a five-dot ellipses at the end, and a two-dotter in the middle, and no apostrophes in sight. God bless him.

9. Tom Aspinall — UFC heavyweight champion (Prev: 5)

You feel for Aspinall at this point. In the prime of his career, he is now forced to: A) cough up the heavyweight title he waited so long to earn; B) worry about his vision returning to him in full; and C) watch the man who poked his eyes, Ciryl Gane, become the "undisputed" heavyweight champion of the world in the snap of a finger. It going to be a rough few months ahead for the pride of Salford.

10. Arman Tsurukyan — UFC lightweight contender (Prev: NR)

He mingles with influencers, flies around on private jets and here's guessing he has a caviar spoon in his silverware drawers at home. But the thing he has made undeniable is that he's the No. 1 contender at lightweight . Mauricio Ruffy is an imposing human being, and Arman flattened him with the kind of elbows that even Justin Gaethje felt in his temples.

(Others receiving votes: Carlos Ulberg, Alexandre Pantoja, Ciryl Gane, Alex Pereira, Max Holloway, Khamzat Chimaev)

1. Valentina Shevchenko — Former UFC flyweight champion (Prev: 1)

It's a bummer that the pound-for-pound best had to vacate her title so that others could get a shot at the belt. But here's guessing Valentina will weigh heavily over the festivities at UFC 332 in Salt Lake, given that Natalia Silva and Wang Cong are, effectively, fighting for a stolen accessory. Until one of them beats Shevchenko, there will be mumblings as to the legitimacy of the feat.

2. Kayla Harrison — UFC bantamweight champion (Prev: 2)

Well, Kayla has a date and location on the books, which is Nov. 14 at UFC 334, at 4 Pennsylvania Plaza (Madison Square Garden). Dana White is already chirping about her fight with Amanda Nunes being the "greatest women's MMA fight of all time," and that's not hyperbole. Harrison's credentials stack up against Nunes' so high that they become part of the New York skyline.

3. Zhang Weili — Former UFC strawweight champion (Prev: 3)

At age 37, Zhang's out living her best life right now, just soaking up the spoils of being ex-champion, modeling, and generally having fun. For fight fans, this might be a little curious. Will she come back and fight Mackenzie Dern, to try to win back the strawweight title she vacated? Or will she stick around at flyweight? Or will she … do none of the above?

4. Cris Cyborg — PFL featherweight champion (Prev: 4)

Cyborg got tested a little bit by Ketlen Vieira in what was billed as most certainly/probably/maybe her last MMA fight. Yet before she could even make it to the exits, there she was sitting alongside her old pal Scott Coker, a celebrated "Cyborg whisperer," for the launch of the new Ki MMA . Will she return? Per the Magic 8 Ball: "All Signs Say Yes."

5. Dakota Ditcheva — PFL flyweight contender (Prev: 5)

Ditcheva beat Denise Kielholtz, yet when we say she did so handily it's an unfortunate pun. Ditcheva says she not only rebroke her hand in the fight, but that she broke her hands , plural, which is about devastating of a blow as she's taken in her career. How long it takes her to fully mend remains to be seen, but it's been a rough couple of years since she was Uncrowned's surprise 2024 Fighter of the Year.

6. Natalia Silva — UFC flyweight contender (Prev: 6)

Maybe it was anticlimactic, but it's not Silva's fault that she's being thrust into a main event at UFC 331. Silva has done nothing but win over the past few years, and she would've gladly punched Shevchenko's face if that was the one made to appear in front of her in Salt Lake. As it happens, it'll be Wang Cong's face she punches, and we'll tell you this — Silva doesn't discriminate.

7. Mackenzie Dern — UFC strawweight champion (Prev: 7)

All is quiet for Dern in the aftermath of her first title defense against Gillian Robertson. There are some names coming up the rungs at strawweight who might kick up a commotion — such as Fatima Kline and Denise Gomes — but Dern's more immediate concern might be Zhang, should the former champ decide she wants her belt back. Good news for Dern is she has final say.

8. Amanda Nunes — UFC bantamweight contender (Prev: NR)

It wasn't all that long ago that Nunes was the women's pound-for-pound queen — and really, she's a win away from reclaiming that spot. That fight with Kayla Harrison is perhaps the biggest of Nunes' career since Cyborg in terms of straight legacy, because who else is out there for her? To beat Harrison would be the cherry on top for the women's GOAT.

9. Seika Izawa — Former RIZIN super atomweight champion (Prev: 9)

She vacated the RIZIN super atomweight title in April after learning of her pregnancy, so it's going to be a minute before we see the Japanese sensation again. Not to be a UFC snob, but it would be fun to see her compete there as a strawweight upon her return. Also, if you haven't done so, check out Drake Riggs' feature on the Japanese sensation!

10. Alexa Grasso — UFC flyweight contender (Prev: NR)

She left Maycee Barber looking dead on the canvas a few months back, which was an impressive thing to do in itself, but to double-down and dominate Manon Fiorot? OK, Alexa, you have our attention. Grasso will be in consideration for "Comeback Fighter of the Year" in a few months, if for no other reason than she looks to be on a warpath to take back all that is hers, and she'll destroy entire cities if she has to.

(Others receiving votes: Tatiana Suarez, Manon Fiorot, Erin Blanchfield, Fatima Kline, Virna Jandiroba, Liz Carmouche)

articles.title: Dana White niega cualquier polémica con los guantes de Gaethje
articles.standfirst: El mandamás de la UFC ha salido al paso de las declaraciones de Topuria en las que dejaba caer que el peleador estadounidense pudo hacer trampas
articles.summary: El mandamás de la UFC ha salido al paso de las declaraciones de Topuria en las que dejaba caer que el peleador estadounidense pudo hacer trampas
articles.body: Ilia Topuria ya tiene lo que buscaba. 'El Matador' ha vuelto al ojo público por todo lo alto, y la semana pasada puso un tuit en el que afirmaba que para la revancha con Justin Gaethje mandaría revisar bien sus guantillas por si tenían algo raro. Lo que en un principio parecía un tuit aislado ha acabado siendo la comidilla de todo el mundo de las MMA, incluido Dana White, que ha negado rotundamente que el nuevo campeón de peso ligero hiciese trampa. El pasado 14 de julio, Gaethje asestó a 'El Matador' su primera derrota profesional y le fracturó la nariz y los dos orbitales gracias a un plan que ejecutó a la perfección para cumplir el sueño de toda su carrera y convertirse en campeón indiscutido del peso ligero. Al ver el rostro de Ilia las teorías conspiranoicas comenzaron a salir a la luz, y una de ellas afirmaba que Justin se metió algo en sus guantillas para golpear más fuerte. A pesar de que ya ha pasado mucho tiempo, Topuria se sumó a la broma el otro día para provocar una reacción, y ha sido el propio Dana White -jefe de la UFC- el que ha salido a desmentirle tras el UFC 331 realizado este pasado fin de semana. "El jefe de la Comisión Atlética de California, probablemente el mejor que haya, estaba ahí. Además, había inspectores viendo cómo se ponía las vendas y las guantillas. No pasó nada con las guantillas de Gaethje". El propio Gaethje salió al paso rápidamente preguntándole si esa era la excusa que se le había ocurrido tras dos meses desaparecido, aunque más tarde se mostró abierto a darle la revancha después de semanas y semanas en las que afirmó que el peleador hispanogeorgiano no se lo merecía. De la misma forma, el propio jefe de la Comisión Atlética desmintió a 'El Matador', por lo que su mensaje se ha propagado hasta los altos mandos. Ahora está en manos de la UFC tomar una decisión, y ver si su misión llega a buen puerto o le toca volver a ganarse la oportunidad titular con otra pelea entre medias.

articles.summary: After his stunning knockout win over Gable Steveson at UFC 331, Sean Sharaf has his own trading card.
articles.body:
After his stunning knockout win over Gable Steveson at UFC 331, Sean Sharaf has his own trading card.

Topps announced Monday that the moment Sharaf knocked out Stevenson will be made into Sharaf's first official trading card.

Steveson came into the fight as a heavy favorite following a very strong start to his MMA career, but moments after the fight began, Steveson's upward trajectory changed shifted. Sharaf knocked him out in 12 seconds, marking one of the fastest wins ever in a UFC heavyweight fight.

Steveson is one of the more exciting prospects in recent UFC memory, while Sharaf has flown mostly under the radar throughout his career, with just two UFC fights under his belt before the bout with Steveson.

Now, Sharaf has made a name for himself with a massive upset win, and he also has a new trading card to commemorate the moment.

articles.title: Jon Jones Explains Gable Steveson Leaving Octagon After 12-Second KO Loss at UFC 331
articles.summary: After his stunning knockout loss to Sean Sharaf at UFC 331, Gable Steveson quickly exited the ring before the winner's hand could be raised.
articles.body:
After his stunning knockout loss to Sean Sharaf at UFC 331, Gable Steveson quickly exited the ring before the winner's hand could be raised.

While the move could be seen by some as poor sportsmanship, Jon Jones, Steveson's mentor, said he advised Steveson to leave early to make sure he was healthy.

Even in knockout situations, it's a bit uncommon for fights to leave the Octagon as fast as Steveson did.

"You cannot be a great winner but then an ungrateful loser, and I think that was bad by Steveson," UFC commentator Daniel Cormier said after Steveson left the ring.

It certainly wasn't a good look from Steveson, but Jones' statement perhaps sheds some light on the situation. In future losses, it might be best for Steveson to stick around for the post-fight formalities.

Steveson, 26, was a collegiate wrestler and Olympic gold medalist who made the transition to MMA last year, and he's been pegged as one of the rising stars in the sport. He won his first four professional fights, including his UFC debut against Elisha Ellison in July.

But not long into his second UFC fight, much of the hype surrounding Steveson vanished. He was a heavy favorite against Sharaf, but lost in just 12 seconds, marking one of the fastest heavyweight finishes in UFC history.

Sharaf wasn't exactly a big name in the world of UFC coming into the fight. He had a 5-2 record but had lost his only two UFC fights before facing Steveson, making the win all the more surprising.

Steveson will surely be back on a main card soon, but the loss to Sharaf perhaps served as a humbling moment early in his career.

articles.standfirst: El debate sobre si los robots terminarán dominando a la humanidad se puso a prueba con un combate de MMA entre un influencer y un Terminator
articles.summary: El debate sobre si los robots terminarán dominando a la humanidad se puso a prueba con un combate de MMA entre un influencer y un Terminator
articles.body: El influencer Frankie Lapenna, sensación estadounidense de las redes sociales con más de 3 millones de seguidores en Instagram, recibió una paliza frente a un robot de 1,80 metros de altura en una pelea de MMA (Artes Marciales Mixtas) que fue promocionada como como la primera pelea entre un humano y un robot. El 'Rekbot' de Rek Robotics, que se asemeja a un T-800 de la franquicia cinematográfica 'Terminator', y el influencer se encerraron en una jaula para pelear en el combate 'Human vs Terminator' (Humano contra Terminator). "Me da miedo por ti", le dijo un hombre a Lapenna antes de pegarse con el robot. Lapenna logró conectar varios golpes al robot, pero el 'Rekbot' terminó derribando al influencer con una patada voladora. El famoso influencer, que terminó magullado y dolorido, cayó desplomado sobre la lona y no pudo volver a ponerse en pie. La pelea tuvo un gran seguimiento en redes sociales, y provoó comentarios como "que se joda la UFC, quiero ver más de esto", "¿de dónde sacó el valor esta persona?
